Radiology Department | Tergooi MC | 10 January 2025 | Multiparametric MRI of the Prostate
Clinical Context: Re-evaluation of established prostate malignancy. Current prostate-specific antigen stands at 7.9 ng/mL. Initial imaging yielded a PI-RADS 4 classification.
Findings: The gland exhibits marked enlargement, occupying 123.0 mL in total volume. Within the peripheral zone, specifically the right mid-gland, a focal zone of restricted diffusion measures 18 × 14 × 16 mm. T2-weighted sequences show pronounced hypointensity alongside early enhancement on dynamic contrast studies. Diffusion-weighted imaging corroborates severe restriction with diminished ADC values. The transition zone demonstrates moderate benign prostatic hyperplasia without suspicious focal areas. Seminal vesicles appear normal. There is no extracapsular extension nor suspicious lymphadenopathy. Bladder and rectal contours are intact.
Impression: PI-RADS 4 lesion localized to the right mid-gland peripheral zone.
Prostate volume 123.0 mL.
PSA density 0.07 ng/mL/mL.
csPCa predicted probability 0.76090467.

previous_notes.text: Attendance at clinic focused on established prostate carcinoma. Serum prostate-specific antigen measured 6.4 ng/mL, representing an increase from the 2.6 ng/mL baseline established in late 2022. Lower urinary tract symptoms remain unchanged, scoring 8 on the IPSS scale. Pedal exercise continues without interruption. Renal parameters show no deviation.
